title: Man shot by cops in Edmonton bank robbery dies
article: The man shot dead at the scene of a south side bank heist had a history with the law, suggest court documents.

The suspect, identified as 24-year-old Mike Benjamin Grisch, was last jailed in June 2010 when he plead guilty to weapons charges dating back to March of that year - where he was found to be in possession of a handgun.
As part of his plea agreement, several charges were dropped, he was ordered to submit a DNA sample for the national databank and he was banned from possessing weapons for ten years.

The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) was called in to investigate the 2 p.m. police shooting during an armed robbery inside Canadian Western Bank, 21 Avenue and 99 Street, at South Edmonton Common on Tuesday.
Two responding officers fired multiple shots at the 24 year old who was armed with a handgun. He was transported to hospital in critical condition, but died of his injuries Wednesday morning.
Investigators say they can't confirm at this point if Grisch fired his weapon at the officers.

ASIRT investigated two fatal Edmonton Police Service shootings in 2011. ASIRT launched an investigation in February 2011 after 17-year-old Cyrus Green was shot three times by an Edmonton city police officer.
Green was killed following a string of armed muggings near the Coliseum LRT station and 118 Avenue.
And Kinling Robin Fire, 49, was shot by Edmonton city police in March 2011. Fire was shot twice by police at 10007 155 St., and later died of his wounds.
He was carrying an eight-inch steel bar and ran towards an officer before being fatally shot in a back alley near a west-end apartment complex.
In both cases, the officers involved were cleared of any wrong doing by ASIRT.
